rows.Incident Description: The guest was unhappy because there were too many children in the pool, which made it hard to swim in lap swim lane.
rows.Subject: 1701 | Mr. Eli Carmona | Service Quality Spa
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
UPDATE: 1/4 (By FOM)
Guest that was affected was actually Mr. Li (Room 1217,  checked out 1/3),  not 1701 Mr. Carmona.
FOM apologized for the misunderstanding to Mr. Carmona for the wrong information that was shared to him.  

Action:
The guest swam in the pool for about 30 minutes,  calmly left a comment at the pool counter,  and then left the pool area.
Spa Mgr was unable to talk with the guest in person at the time, thus,  a message and an amenity were sent to the guest room.
Spa Mgr will contact the guest again on the 2nd of January.

Investigation:
At the time of the incident,  9 children (#907,  908,  2305,  1101,  1015) and their family members were in the pool,  which made the area very crowded.
Two instructors watched the pool the whole time and quickly stopped unsafe actions,  like diving or going into the Lap Swim Lane. Still,  with so many children,  it was not possible to stop every unsafe action.

Make it Right:
-When there are many children,  guide them to an area away from the Lane.
- Besides instructors,  have Spa Attendants help watch the pool.
-Use whistles only when needed,  and follow these steps: First,  give a verbal warning. Second,  blow a short whistle. Third,  blow the whistle several times and move the person to a different area.

rows.Subject: 2015 | Mr. Veysel Erdem | Checked in to occupied dirty room
rows.Investigation/Follow Up 1: Checked in to occupied dirty room
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
[Action]
- After escorting,  FDA informed DM that room was occupied,  guest chose to wait in party room 2014. 
- DM immediately called guest room #2015 Mr. Erdem and apologized for the inconvenience. Guest was calm. 
- At 13:55,  Guest came to FD to check-out. DM personally apologized again and gave business card for further assistance. Guest remained calm and understanding.

[Investigation]
- At 11:40,  an accompany of Mr. Hara arrived and had three rooms which were assigned into #2013,  2014,  2015. Only room 2013 & 2014 were inspected and 2015 was dirty status and occupied. 
- The accompany requested to have 3rd room (#2015) to be ready immediately and FDA offered to look for other availability and found new room,  to change assign from 2015 to 2017.
- However,  FDA mistakenly changed the assignment in the reservation screen of due out guest #2015 Mr. Erdem,  instead of due in Mr. Hara,  and also changed #2015's room status from dirty to inspected.
- Due to changing room status to Inspected,  FDS checked in Mr. Hara into #2015 and escorted the accompany to #2015. 
- When FDA opened the door #2015,  FDA found guest was in room and reported to DM. 
- After entering the occupied room 2015,  assignment for Mr. Hara was changed to #2002. DM apologized the accompany and escorted to new room #2002 in person. The accompany was calm and understanding. 

[Make It Right]
- DM talked to related FD agent importance of carefully checking room assignment.

9:07 Guest came FD to check-out
9:08 DM called HSK coordinator to deliver the pajama to FD
9:12 DM called HSK coordinator and changed request deliver pajama to room (wife requested packing in room).
9:17 Guest informed DM wife still waiting

9:21 Guest asked DM again,  DM called HSKAMGR

rows.Incident Description: PST Roppongi contacted CON and advised that the guest was a no-show. Upon review, CON confirmed that the reservation was made with the Roppongi location; however, the confirmation indicated the Higashi-Azabu branch.
rows.Subject: 2305 | Mr. Akira Akuto | Incorrect booking Concierge
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Update : 1/3 20:00 Guest replied as below,  
"We ended up ordering take away pizza from higashi Azabu and eating in the park outside.
Mistakes happen. And no need to apologize!"
CON has sent an apology letter and amenity to the room. PTK will cover the cancellation fee of PST Roppongi,  it is not shared with the guest.  

Action : CON immediately tried to contact the customer,  however could not reach. While speaking with both the Higashi-Azabu and Roppongi restaurants,  it was confirmed that the guest was unable to secure seating at the Higashi-Azabu location and therefore opted for take-away. However,  a no-show penalty of JPY 6, 000 per person (total JPY 26, 400) was incurred at the Roppongi restaurant.
CON has emailed the guest requesting to speak with them upon their return to the hotel and is currently attempting to make contact. 

Investigation : 
Jan 2,  11:30 – CON 1 received a request from the guest to make a reservation,  with the Higashi-Azabu branch as the first preference and Roppongi as the alternative if unavailable.
Jan 2,  13:30 – CON 2 contacted the restaurants and secured a reservation at the Roppongi branch,  as the Higashi-Azabu location was not available. However,  the vendor name in the system was not updated accordingly.
Jan 3,  17:15 – CON received a call reporting a no-show and subsequently identified the discrepancy noted above.

Make it right : It is necessary to review the reservation process and,  together with the relevant staff,  reassess how similar incidents can be prevented in the future. Going forward,  an itinerary should be created for each reservation and carefully reviewed to ensure that all information provided to the guest is accurate.

rows.Incident Description:
1. Guest disputed paying Zuicho's cancellation of JPY210,000 for 1/3 and gave negative feedback about concierge to FD. 

2. Guest wanted to go to Morton’s The Steakhouse on Jan 3. Concierge told him it is full, and he walked in that same night, and it was empty. 
Concierge recommendation was not met the guest expectation.
rows.Subject: 1713 | Mr. Alberto Torrado | Service Quality Concierge
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
[Action]
DM sincerely apologized and expressed concern for the guest. The guest mentioned that they did not confirm the booking at Zuicho. As a result,  a penalty of JPY 210, 000 was incurred.
The guest raised this concern with HM.

[Investigation]
- Zuicho : Concierge received the restaurant request on December 30 and immediately communicated with the Torrado family regarding availability and requirements. The reservation was successfully secured,  and CON sent the official confirmation on the same day. This confirmation clearly included Zuicho’s cancellation policy and the applicable penalties.

Despite this,  the guest later stated that they were not aware of the cancellation policy and claimed they had never confirmed the reservation. To address this discrepancy,  CON shared the complete email correspondence record with HM,  which shows that the reservation was confirmed in writing and that the cancellation policy had been properly communicated in advance.

- Morton : CON received the guest’s request on January 3 to secure a reservation at Morton’s of Chicago for 6 guests at 20:00. CON contacted the restaurant to check availability. Based on the information provided by the restaurant at that time,  CON informed the guest that Morton’s was fully booked for the evening. As an alternative,  CON proposed Wolfgang’s Steakhouse,  which had availability at the requested time.

However,  the guest later reported that they visited Morton’s directly that same night (time unknown) and found the restaurant empty,  expressing dissatisfaction and stating that the concierge should have the connections to accommodate last‑minute reservations.  According to our investigation,  Concierge (CON) contacted Morton’s at the time of the guest’s request and was informed that the restaurant was indeed fully booked. CON relayed this information accurately to the guest. We also confirmed that The Peninsula Tokyo has an established hotline with Morton’s,  and CON followed the proper procedure when checking availability.
 
[Make It Right]
- CM shared all information with HM and ADOR
- ADOR/HM will contact guest through e-mail.

rows.Incident Description: The guest went to the restaurant despite a prior cancellation due to miscommunication
rows.Subject: 905 | Mrs. Joanna Cabangon | Miscommunication Concierge
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
【Action】
-After receiving a Pen Chat message from the guest that Ningyocho Imahan Ginza was fully booked for dinner and the restaurant could not find any reservation under the guest name,  CON called the guest to apologize for the inconvenience and immediately offered nearby alternatives.

-CON offered to arrange a hotel car to pick up the guest from the restaurant; however,  the guest had already found another nearby restaurant and happy to dine there instead.

-CON prepared amenities and an apology message card to be placed in the room to welcome the guest back after dinner.

【Investigation】
1/5:
-The guest requested cancellation of the restaurant reservation via Pen Chat.
-CON attempted to contact the restaurant multiple times but was unable to reach them.
-CON informed the guest that we would follow up with the restaurant to cancel the reservation without a fee.

1/6:
-CON successfully contacted the restaurant and canceled the reservation without a fee.
-CON did not update the guest via Pen Chat after the cancellation was completed.

1/7:
-The guest contacted Pen Chat to ask for the dinner time,  believing the reservation was still active.
-GCC replied on behalf of CON,  advising that the reservation was at 7:00 PM,  and the guest proceeded to the restaurant.
-GCC checked the task in Alice but did not notice that the status had already been marked as CXLD (Cancelled).

Make it Right: 
-Ops Mgr reminded the CON staff in charge to clearly communicate and update the guest after completing any cancellation task.
-GCC Mgr conducted refresher training for GCC staff on how to properly check and verify task status in Alice.

rows.Incident Description: Received email from guest after check out which informing his disappointment about taxi he had took from the hotel to cruise terminal.
rows.Subject: 1114 | Mr. Kevin Wong | Taxi
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Email content: 
We checked out of the hotel at 11:30 and expressly told the door staff (and presented the printed address) where we were headed (that is to join the Seabourn Encore ship at the Tokyo International Cruise terminal).  Enroute,  we had to wake up the taxi driver who had fallen asleep at a red light.  Worse,  he did not know where to drop us off and instead stopped at an intersection somewhere near,  but not at the passenger cruise terminal.
We elected to leave the taxi after paying the full rate and used our internet to obtain an Uber that brought us to the terminal directly.
Please convey our disappointment to the front desk and bell team and make sure that they use taxi drivers that do not pose a security risk (of falling asleep) and better yet,  know where to drop off your guests.

Action:
-GSM immediately contacting to taxi company and reported the incident and lodged a strong protest. 
-It was strongly conveyed that the driver will be prohibited from waiting for guests at the hotel going forward.
-GSM sent apology email to guest. 

Investigation:
-Guest took a taxi which was standing by from the side street. This taxi company is not familiar with doorman team. 
-The doorman confirmed that the cruise terminal guide held by the guest clearly indicated the address. He instructed the driver to enter this address into the GPS but full address could not be set thus he verbally told the driver to go to Tokyo Cruise terminal for sure. 
-Taxi Company conducted a fact-check with the driver,  who acknowledged that the guest addressed him while waiting at a traffic light and admitted that,  when the destination failed to display properly on the GPS,  he chose to let the guest off.

Make it Right:
Drivers must be clearly informed of the destination and their understanding confirmed. Should the driver appear uncertain,  arranging for the guest to switch to another taxi should be considered.

1/12 (16:13)

We trusted your team to ensure quality,  and that trust was not met."

1/12 (16:30)
・CON MGR contacted KRO regarding the guest’s dissatisfaction. The assigned guide is a veteran,  licensed professional who has served PTK guests since 2023 and has handled 186 private tours for PTK over the past three years.
・Based on KRO’s discussion with the guide,  the guest may have perceived a lack of confidence due to the guide’s verbal tone,  body language,  and frequent consultation with the taxi driver. This possibly gave the impression that the guide was unfamiliar with Nikko and relied on the driver for answers.
・Additionally,  the guest,  traveling with a 1 -year-old baby and a 5-year-old child,  required extra time for diaper changes. The guide’s perceived urgency may have felt pushy,  leading the guest to conclude that time management during the tour was inadequate.

【Make it right】
・KRO has confirmed that this guide will not be assigned to any future PTK guests unless a repeat guest specifically requests her by name.

rows.Subject: 2202 | Ms. Anna Sasha Solomon | Dietary Restriction Allergy Lobby
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Action
A staff member mistakenly served multigrain toast containing butter to a guest with a dairy allergy.

Investigation
Due to unclear input instructions for recording allergy information on the order slip,  both the kitchen staff and the DUP staff mistakenly believed that only one guest had a dairy allergy. In fact,  there were two guests with a dairy allergy.

Make it right
Lobby MGR immediately apologized,  provided his business card,  and informed the guests that they could contact us at any time if needed. The guests appreciated for the follow‑up.
The system of inputting order has been changed to reflect the allergy of each seat and avoid reoccurrence.

Internal
We will update the method for entering allergy information on the order slip as attached picture and communicate about the changes to both kitchen and service team.

rows.Incident Description:

rows.Subject: 7F Reservations | Mr. Robert Demeter | Miscommunication
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Action:
RES SV took over the guest’s call,  apologized for the miscommunication,  clarified room capacity and rates,  and attempted to de‑escalate the situation.
Case was escalated to RES AM and Director of Revenue.
The guest claimed the average rate of 3+1 promo (PGMORE4) was offered to him as the BAR rate. After internal discussion,  we have approved the rate the guest claimed for. A confirmation email with the honored rate was sent to the guest on the same day.

Investigation：
1/21 3:15 AM 
FD agent shared details from a night phone call with the guest via the FD–RES Teams.

1/21 Morning 
RES morning-shift agent marked the message with a “thumbs up, ” but it was not verbally communicated during the morning briefing. As a result,  RES team was unaware of the message.

1/21 12:11 PM 
RES replied to an email received from the guest at 3:09 AM,  which only stated “Thank You” without further details.

1/21 12:22 PM 
The guest replied,  expressing concern that his information had not been shared internally.

1/21 1:47 PM 
The guest called RES,  and RES SV answered. The guest expressed strong dissatisfaction,  stating that he had already provided his information to the FD agent during the night and that the departments were not communicating properly. He raised his voice and showed visible frustration.
RES SV reviewed the email and FD–RES Teams records,  located the FD agent’s message,  and apologized for the oversight.

Rate Explanation
Because the FD agent’s message contained no rate information,  RES SV provided the correct 3+1 promo rate (JPY 260, 000+++ for 13–17 March,  4 nights including 1 complimentary night).
The guest became upset,  insisting he had been quoted “around JPY 720, 000 total” during the night and believed the booking had already been confirmed.
RES SV explained the 3+1 promo rate mechanics shown on the website (average rate display),  apologized again,  and offered to conduct an internal review and follow up via email.
The guest agreed and ended the call feeling that the matter was being appropriately handled.

1/21 2:08 PM
RES SV updated the FD Team via the FD–RES Teams.

1/21 Afternoon
RES SV reported the case to DM and RES AM.
As it was difficult to verify the exact rate the guest was told during the night,  RES AM instructed SV to escalate to the Director of Revenue to seek the Director’s negotiation and approval on the rate. Due to the time difference and the guest’s request to resolve the matter within the next 2–3 hours.

1/21 Around 6:00 PM
DM contacted RES SV to obtain further information,  which was provided.

1/21 6:23 PM
After receiving approval from the Director of Revenue,  RES SV emailed the guest to confirm that the rate claimed would be honored. (As instructed by the Director,  FD was not informed at this stage)

1/22 8:18 AM
The guest sent a thank-you email expressing appreciation for the resolution.

Make It Right:
Ensure all future related FD–RES communication messages are reviewed and verbally shared during daily morning briefings.
Continue providing training to ensure the FD team can communicate rates accurately.

rows.Incident Description: The guest expressed dissatisfaction with the Italian restaurant recommendation (Il Boccalone) due to the atmosphere not meeting his expectations and requested an alternative upscale restaurant.
rows.Subject: 2215 | Mr. Pablo Funtanet Mange | Dissatisfactory Recommendation Concierge
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Action:
•	At 18:14,  he called CON from the restaurant stating dissatisfaction and left the venue.
•	He requested Niko Romito,  which was fully booked.
•	CON offered Gucci Osteria as an alternative,  which he accepted.
•	At 18:25,  CON informed him,  providing the address directly to the taxi driver.

Investigation:
•	At approximately 16:00,  he approached CON requesting Italian restaurant recommendations,  without specifying a particular style.
•	At 16:21,  CON emailed three recommended restaurants: Elio Locanda Italiana,  Piacere,  and Il Boccalone.
•	At 16:39,  CON provided detailed explanations of each restaurant’s concept and atmosphere.
•	At 16:45,  he selected Il Boccalone.
•	At 17:00,  CON sent a confirmation email for Il Boccalone.

CON clearly explained the characteristics and atmosphere of all three recommended restaurants prior to the guest’s selection. Elio Locanda Italiana was introduced as a traditional southern Italian,  home-style restaurant; Piacere as an upscale contemporary Italian restaurant with seasonal Japanese influences; and Il Boccalone as an old-school trattoria with bold flavors and classic Italian flair.

However,  after visiting the restaurant,  he expressed strong dissatisfaction,  mainly regarding the atmosphere,  and indicated a preference for a significantly more upscale dining experience,  suggesting that although he initially appeared open to suggestions and did not clearly specify an upscale preference,  their actual expectation aligned more with high-end fine dining rather than a casual or traditional trattoria-style restaurant.

Make It Right:
•	CON extended an apologies and offered potential reimbursement for taxi fee inconvenience.
•	CON will follow up and ask him the details of his feedback.
•	The guest may reach out with the receipt of taxi for the reimbursement.

rows.Incident Description: Concierge has mistakenly disclosed the Surprise cake arrangement with the husband for gender reveal.
rows.Subject: 1212 | Mr. Michael James Murphy | Miscommunication Concierge
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Action : 
•CON immediately apologized to Mr. Murphy for the confusion and misunderstanding regarding the gender reveal cake. •CON explained the situation to Mrs. Murphy’s sister,  Mrs.Gina,  who had intended the cake as a surprise,  and assured her that we would take all necessary steps to recover the situation and ensure the surprise is successfully arranged for Mrs. Murphy.
• CON confirmed who should be the main point of contact for the cake arrangement moving forward.
• Mr. Murphy confirmed that he would be the primary contact going forward. Mrs.Gina also replied that she would let Mr. Murphy communicate with CON directly to avoid further miscommunication.
•CON reassured both of them that the gender reveal cake for Mrs. Murphy will be arranged with the utmost care tonight.

- The gender reveal cake will be ready at Guest Services by 19:00,  timed with their departure for dinner at Teppanyaki 10 Shibuya,  with complimentary hotel Alphard service arranged from GS. In addition,  CON prepared a newborn gift (a Japanese hakama-style baby outfit) with a decorative balloon arrangement and a handwritten Sakura congratulations card from the entire concierge team,  to be set up before their return.

Investigation : 
• CON received a gender reveal cake request for Mr. and Mrs. Murphy from Mrs. Murphy’s sister,  Gina,  via email from the U.S.
• While the cake was being arranged,  Mr. Murphy (husband) visited the Concierge Desk to ask about the cake request sent by Mrs.Gina.
• At that time,  the staff member on duty assumed the surprise was only for Mrs. Murphy (wife) and did not realize that Mr. Murphy was also not supposed to know the gender.
• After Mr. Murphy’s first visit,  the same staff member received a call from the grandfather,  Mr. Dzama,  requesting to change tonight’s dinner plan from HFT to an outside restaurant.
• Mr. Murphy then visited the desk again,  mentioning that Mr. Dzama had already requested to cancel HFT,  and asked whether the outside restaurant could prepare the cake instead. The staff advised that she would check and follow up via email.
• After reviewing the details,  the staff replied to the email thread including both Mrs. Gina and Mr. Murphy,  explaining that the outside restaurant could not accommodate the cake request at short notice,  but Room Service could arrange it. The email included a photo of the cake and described the cake as having “blue cream” inside.
• CON subsequently received an email from Mr. Murphy stating that he was not supposed to know the gender.

Make it right : 
• For future sensitive requests (e.g.,  surprises,  proposals,  gender reveals),  managers will ensure staff confirm:
-the intended recipient(s) of the surprise
-the main primary contact person (who should / should not be included in the email thread)
• A manager will use this incident as a case study and conduct a short 1-on-1 coaching session with all team members to reinforce discretion and handling of sensitive requests.
• The staff member involved has already been coached in person by CM.

Investigation:
-Coffee delay

-Bacon with egg dish
At the same time,  another table had ordered an egg dish with bacon,  and while adding bacon to that dish,  bacon was mistakenly added to this egg dish as well.
Without noticing the error,  both the dish-up staff and the chef signed the allergy sheet,  and the dish was served to the guest.

However,  they failed to reconfirm the egg dish that was served afterward.

Make It Right:
-Coffee delay

Action:

-Guests raised concerns regarding the room rate discrepancy with LM. LM contacted RSVN team to conduct further investigation.
-In the meantime,  the guest’s sibling (not an in-house guest) assisted by communicating in Japanese on behalf of the guest.

[14:35]

Investigation:
[2/18]
-Upon check-in,  FDSV did not inform the guest of the room rate at the time of arrival.

[2/22]

1st room: #1215 – The original rate was JPY 150, 000+++ per night. The rate was adjusted to JPY 140, 000+++ when the length of stay was changed to four nights in June,  and the lower rate was honored at that time. Subsequently,  the stay was amended back to three nights at the last minute; however,  the JPY 140, 000+++ rate was retained.
2nd room: #1210 – The rate of JPY 150, 000+++ per night had been maintained since the original reservation made in April 2025. Although the length of stay was modified in August,  the rate of JPY 150, 000+++ remained unchanged at that time.
3rd room (This room was no issued): #1218 – The booking followed a similar amendment pattern as noted above,  1st room. rows.Incident Description: The item was pre-paid by TA as a gift, but was mistakenly charged again at check-out.
rows.Subject: 919 | Ms. Paetongtarn Shinawatra | 625,000 Consortia | Billing Issue Dispute Charge Concierge
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
【Action】
・TA called Ops Mgr requesting an immediate refund,  as the guest was charged for the strawberry Daifuku at check-out despite it being pre-paid (double charge case).
・Ops Mgr apologized to TA and instructed FDA to refund the amount to the guest’s credit card immediately.
・As a gesture of apology,  the full amount (JPY 7, 233) will also be refunded to TA’s credit card and covered by PTK.

【Investigation】
・CON purchased 16 strawberry Daifuku on the C/I date and sent a payment link to TA in advance.
・As per current procedure,  CON posted all pre-paid MISC / PAID OUT items to Window 2 with payment status indicated in the cashier comments.
・CON did not update the comment in Shiji to “Received” after payment was completed.

【Make It Right】
・CON will realign the internal cashier posting procedure for both in-house and future guest pre-paid cases with the FD team.
・Previously,  all pre-paid cases were posted to Window 2,  creating a risk of mixing with other MISC charges/Hotel Credits and causing confusion at final billing.
・Moving forward,  for any pre-paid cases by TA or GOA:
1) The amount must be posted to Window 1.
2) The posting comment must be clearly stated in the “Internal Remark” section as:
“PB TA via PL (Order ID)” or “Self-prepaid via PL (Order ID)”
This ensures both CON and FD are aligned and prevents future double-charging cases.

rows.Incident Description: The spa treatment booking for two at 11:00 on March 1, made through the Concierge, was not on the Spa reservation system.

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:

When informed of the incident,  the Spa Manager attempted to contact the guests by phone but received no answer. The Manager then delivered a written apology and a Spa gift to their room. The letter invited the guests to return for a complimentary treatment. The team is now awaiting the guests’ response to arrange a new booking.

>>Complimentary spa treatment 55 min for two has been booked for March 3rd at 10:00 AM. The fee is waived as an apology. The spa manager greeted them at the counter and explained the investigation results. They appreciated the thorough investigation and were pleased to have a massage before departure.

[Investigation] 
The March 1,  11:00 AM spa treatment for two guests,  originally intended for Ms. Newman in #1412,  was mistakenly booked under room 1415 for Mrs. Dag Guven and Sebnem. When Mrs. Dag Guven in #1415 reported she had not made the reservation,  the booking was cancelled without further verification,  which led to the loss of the original reservation.

-Failure to verify guest's name identity at the time of booking creation. Incorrect reliance on room number only,  leading to misattribution of the booking.
-The cancellation was processed without cross-checking other reservations or consulting Concierge records.

[Make it Right]
-Always confirm the guest’s full name for bookings received through Concierge,  Front Desk,  or external calls.
-When receiving a cancellation request,  do not cancel a booking just because the guest says they do not recall making it. Always conduct two-point verification by checking with both Concierge and Front Desk before processing the cancellation.

rows.Incident Description:

Guest made a complaint at the concierge desk regarding the behavior of two hotel staff members.
rows.Subject: 2312 | Mr. Gurkan Teoman | Staff Attitude Housekeeping
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Action:
Assistant Chief Concierge listened to the guest’s complaint. The guest explained that when he was about to leave his room,  two hotel staff members came out from the neighboring room and bowed to him. The guest perceived this as a sign of respect and reciprocated by bowing in the same manner. However,  it seems that the staff members’ reaction was perceived by the guest as mocking his gesture.

Assistant Chief Concierge offered a sincere apology,  which the guest accepted. During the remainder of his stay,  the guest requested that those two staff members not enter his room.

Investigation:
18:10
The staff were setting up amenities in Room 2313.
After leaving the room,  they encountered the guest in the hallway. While politely avoiding the guest,  they greeted him. The guest then stood directly in front of them,  motionless,  and bowed in the same manner. The staff,  acknowledging the guest’s gesture,  smiled and returned the greeting.

As the staff prepared to leave,  the guest called out to them,  saying,  “I am also showing respect,  so do not laugh.” The staff apologized deeply,  but the guest clicked his tongue and returned to his room.
(It is believed that the guest then went to the concierge desk.)

Make it Right:
After the TD service was completed and the apology letter and amenities had been arranged,  the guest returned,  and AHKM offered a direct apology.
The guest commented on the cultural differences between his country and Japan,  noting that,  in this instance,  the staff’s behavior appeared negative from his perspective.
AHKM explained that the hotel staff did not intend to behave in any disrespectful manner,  but acknowledged that if it was perceived that way,  it was a shortcoming on our part,  and offered a sincere apology.
The guest accepted the apology,  noting that different countries have different cultures and that this incident was not significant,  asking that it be forgotten.

Additionally,  after confirming with the two staff members involved,  they stated that they smiled because the guest had intentionally bowed to them and that they did not behave in any rude or disrespectful manner. It is believed that their smile may have been perceived by the guest as mocking.

Per the guest’s request,  HSKP will ensure that these two staff members will not enter the guest’s room until he checks out.

rows.Incident Description: The guest ordered a medium-rare burger, but unfortunately, the cooking time did not meet the guest’s requested doneness.
rows.Subject: 1401 | Mr. Leslie Frank Weisbrod | Request not met Lobby 340000JPY
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Action:
The guest placed an order with the server for a medium‑rare burger accompanied by French fries. Once the food was served,  the guest began eating the burger. Shortly after starting the meal,  the guest called the Assistant Manager to the table. The guest expressed that the burger’s cooking doneness did not match the medium‑rare level originally requested. The Assistant Manager listened to the guest’s concern and apologized for the inconvenience. The Assistant Manager then instructed the kitchen to prepare a new medium‑rare burger to meet the original request.
However,  upon serving the second burger,  the guest again observed that the cooking doneness did not match the expected medium‑rare level

Investigation:
 The server took the guest’s order for a burger and French fries. However,  during the ordering process,  the server didn't input the requested cooking style (medium-rare) into the order system.
As a result,  the order was sent to the kitchen without any special doneness instruction. Due to the missing doneness request,  the burger was automatically prepared at the standard doneness level. When the dish was served,  the guest began eating and subsequently expressed dissatisfaction,  noting that the burger did not match his original medium‑rare preference. The Assistant Manager apologized to the guest and reordered the burger,  this time specifying medium rare. However,  upon receiving the second burger,  the guest reported that the cooking doneness was medium well,  still not meeting expectations. After the second unsuccessful attempt,  the guest requested to discontinue any further cooking attempts. Instead,  he chose to order dessert.
The guest completed his dessert and finished his wine without further issues.

Make it right:
The Assistant Manager apologized to the guest for the inconvenience caused. As a gesture of goodwill,  both the burger and the dessert were offered complimentary. The guest sincerely appreciated the gesture and expressed satisfaction with the recovery provided.
Following the incident,  the staff were reminded of the correct procedures regarding processed meat and the required cooking styles for burgers. The importance of accurately entering all special requests—especially doneness preferences—into the ordering system was reinforced. The team was also advised that in any situation of uncertainty,  they should consult a senior staff member before making a final decision.

The itinerary had been shared in advance prior to the guest’s arrival.
The request to return to the hotel approximately 10 minutes earlier had been made by the guest herself.

Hi Gareth

Our stay at The Peninsula Tokyo from 2–5 March 2026 was nothing short of exceptional. Having stayed in many of the world’s finest hotels over the years, we do not say this lightly—this property truly stands out for its class, refinement, and remarkable attention to detail.

What impressed us most, however, was the consistency of the service. Every interaction with the staff reflected genuine warmth, professionalism, and pride in what they do. From arrival to departure, we felt looked after in a way that very few hotels manage to achieve.
The Peninsula Tokyo manages to combine grandeur with warmth, elegance with comfort, and world-class service with an unmistakable sense of place. For seasoned travellers accustomed to top-tier hotels around the globe, this stay was truly exceptional.

rows.Incident Description:
Guest called GCC and claimed guest heard some noise from air conditioner. 
At 18:05, the guest called GCC again and mentioned that they were still waiting for HSK and ENG to visit.
rows.Subject: 1914 | Ms. Carla  Damato Salgueiro Barella
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Updated 3/21.
-DM did talk to guest and informed the issue. Guest prefer not to move the room. However,  if guest could not sleep,  she will contact us for sleeping room. Now block 1714.

[Action]
- GCCM apologized to guest and dispatched HSK and ENG to check the noise. 
- DM offered room move and showed new room 1517,  however,  when the AC was turned on,  the same noise occurred in 1517.
- ENG adjusted the midpoint setting from 20°C to 22°C to maintain a consistent output temperature. If the air conditioner maintains a consistent temperature,  the clicking/popping sound caused by metal expansion or contraction should not occur. ENG advised the guest to keep the temperature consistent,  and the guest acknowledged. 
- Guest expressed concern about the sound occurring during the night. DM assured the guest that a quiet sleeping room 1714 would be secured just in case.

[Investigation]
- Banging noise from the AC filter was confirmed.
- The AC filter contains metal components,  and when they are rapidly heated or cooled,  they produce a clicking or popping noise. 
- 17:35: GCC sent HOTSOS to HSK
- 17:42: HSK sent HOTSOS to ENG
- 18:00: HSK and ENG visited room to check
- Guest waited approximately 25 minutes for the visit.

While the guest was out,  ENG adjusted the breeze line to eliminate any clicking/popping noises. Changing the AC temperature will cause noise,  so we need to check the inside of the ceiling after the 26th when the guests check out.

I checked the air conditioner after the guests checked out. There was no noise and the temperature was stable. We think the noise is caused by the metal expansion or contraction inside the ceiling when the air conditioner is turned on and off.

[Make It Right]
- DM will make a courtesy call on 3/21.

rows.Incident Description: PenChat suddenly stopped working properly and our replies to guests were delayed.
rows.Subject: UPDATE/ 1605| Mr. Cassio Motta Mello| JPY210,000| Ad Hoc Group| Reply delay by PenChat due to issue
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
----update 3/23 
While the guest stopped by FD for another matter and DM spoke with the guest directly.
DM apologized in person regarding this issue. During their conversation,  DM had a chance to share that the delay was caused by unexpected maintenance. The guest understood the situation and accepted the explanation.

【Action】
Concierge team quickly made a reservation at the restaurant the guest wanted and was able to have a dinner.
GCCAM sent apology amenity and letter.

【Investigation】
For PenChat
19:35 We suddenly start to becoming unable to access PenChat.
19:47 GCC staff found out that PenChat was under maintenance from the pop‑up message in PenChat.
19:54 Access became possible step by step and the system returned to normal.
**GCCAM emailed ReviewPro to request advance notice whenever maintenance is scheduled and to ask when the system will be fully usable again.
We have not received a reply yet but at the moment the system is usable,  although it sometimes takes a little time to load.

For Mr Mello,  Cassio Motta
19:30 Mr Mello sent a request to book at "Sukiyaki Juniten" at 20:15 for 1person.
19:46 He sent a message asking if we could call the restaurant because he is on the way.
  >> Actually,  the issue had already started when we were exchanging messages earlier,  but we could not inform him about it.
　   From that point,  we were completely unable to send any messages.
19:51 Received a message asking why the request sent at 19:30 had still not been completed.
19:53 GCC informed GST "Sukiyaki Juniten" is fully booked.
20:17 We confirmed that the next restaurant he wants to try is “Moritaya.”
20:23 We updated to him it has been confirmed.
20:35 He send us a message "It's ok. I'm already here"

PenChat system on PC was unstable but we could barely use it on iPhone,  so we tried to contact the guest from there.
However,  we completely missed the timing to inform the guest about the unexpected maintenance is occurring that we could not access the system properly.
After the reservation was confirmed,  Concierge called the guest several times but not answer.


【Make it Right】
We were not informed in advance that this maintenance would take place.
As a future measure,  since PenChat issues occur sometimes,  we will notify guests as soon as we notice that an issue is happening.
There may also be times when we cannot access PenChat at all. In such situations,  we will continue trying other ways to contact the guest,  such as calling them by phone.

DM and EM will send off upon C/O.

rows.Incident Description: GST complained at the CON desk regarding dissatisfaction with their tour guide due to lack of guidance and attention to guests’ needs.
rows.Subject: 2207 | Mr. Jeffrey Griffiths | Direct 354,000 | Service Quality Concierge
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Action taken
CON deeply apologized to GST and thanked her for her feedback and promised to get in touch with the tour operator for further investigation and solution. CON further investigated with KRO and was able to reduce the tour price by 30%.
 
Investigation
09:00 GST was already checking with CON whether the tour guide has already arrived,  however,  CON informed that the tour will start at 10:00 as originally scheduled and the guide will arrive around that time.
09:50 The tour guide arrived and met with GSTs.
14:20 - GST (Mrs. Griffiths) passed by the desk frustrated about their tour guide.
She stated that at some point they got lost and the guide started using google maps which signals unprofessionalism. She also stated that the guide seemed unknowledgeable about Tokyo. Due to this,  they decided to end the tour at 13:50 (1 Hour and 40 minutes early than scheduled). They also reported that the guide did not bother to help them get a taxi back to The Peninsula which made the guest feel that she does not care about the family especially,  it was raining and they had children with them. She also complained that the tour guide arrived exactly at 10:00 leaving them no time to discuss the tour. CON deeply apologized to GST and thanked her for her feedback and promised to get in touch with the tour operator for further investigation and solution.
16:23 Upon checking with KRO,  they reported that The guide prioritized the children’s needs and overall safety under challenging conditions. At peak lunchtime in crowded Harajuku,  the guide used real-time navigation to quickly secure a nearby restaurant,  avoiding a longer walk while the children were hungry. Throughout the day,  the family moved at a very fast pace,  with the mother often walking ahead; the guide’s focus was on maintaining correct navigation and preventing the group from getting lost,  particularly in large areas like Meiji Jingu. Additional strain came from conflicting parental preferences around transportation—walking versus taxis—compounded by rain and limited taxi availability,  resulting in repeated long walks and logistical inefficiencies. After some negotiation,  CON was able to reduce the price by 30% with KRO and GST was very appreciative of the gesture.
 
Make It Right
CON ensured that the guest was well taken care of throughout the day with regards to inquiries and request,  which made the guest really happy and appreciative.
CON also noticed in Alice notes that one of the children,  Ms. Anna Victoria is celebrating her birthday. CON team prepared a cute Hello Kitty birthday card as well as asked helped from RMSVC to deliver a strawberry shortcake tomorrow,  April 1st at 19:00.

rows.Incident Description: The guest commented to the front desk when leaving the room around 6:45 PM tonight that, in the bedroom, there has been a dripping-water-like sound at night for the past two consecutive days.
rows.Subject: 1812 | Mr. Richard Garth Bittar | Noise
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Updated 4/5
-DM met gst upon departure. Guest was in good spirit and requested to not assign same room for him for second booking.

Action：
The guest left at 7:00 PM,  after which an engineer and an HSKP runner went to check the noise.
They listened carefully for about 30 minutes but were unable to hear anything.
After 8:00 PM,  the AHKM also joined and checked again,  at which point they were able to detect a very faint unusual noise.

Investigation：
It was difficult to identify the exact source of the noise; however,  it was determined that it was most likely coming from the AC air outlet.
When the screws securing both ends of the outlet are tightened too firmly,  temperature changes can sometimes cause thermal contraction,  resulting in a clicking sound (similar to water dripping). Therefore,  the engineer slightly loosened the tightly fastened screws on both ends of the AC outlet.
As a result,  the faint noise that had been heard appeared to have disappeared

Make it right：
As soon as the engineer finished the work,  the guest returned to the room. The AHKM apologized and explained the work that had been carried out.
The guest accepted the explanation and apology,  and mentioned that if the noise occurs again tonight,  they will contact us.
If we receive any further comments from the guest tomorrow,  we will address them again during the room cleaning tomorrow.

rows.Incident Description:
April 19th

Due to a driver’s oversleeping, the arranged vehicle (one Toyota HiAce) was not ready at the scheduled pickup time of 10:30 AM.
As a result, the guests departed from PTK at 10:45 AM in three random taxies, accompanied by three hotel attendants, and were able to board the bullet train at 10:59 AM.

Bullet Train: Nozomi No. 371 / 11:09 AM
Vendor: Hinomaru Limousine
Vehicle: Toyota Hi-Ace
Scheduled Pickup Time: 10:30 AM
From: The Peninsula Tokyo
To: Tokyo Station
rows.Subject: 1419 | Mr. Antoni Antoniev Trenchev | Hotel Limousine
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Action & Investigation:

April 19 
10:25 AM
GS was informed by the chauffeur company that the driver had overslept and would not be able to arrive in time for the scheduled pickup. Although we were advised that a replacement vehicle would be dispatched immediately,  it had still not arrived by 10:45 AM.

To ensure the guests could catch the bullet train,  three street taxis were secured. Initially,  two hotel staff members had been arranged to accompany the guests to Tokyo Station; however,  to ensure timely arrival,  three staff members were dispatched.

As there were more than ten pieces of luggage,  the hotel staff also boarded the bullet train with the guests. They assisted by negotiating with station staff to secure sufficient luggage space on behalf of the guests,  which required additional time. One staff member accompanied the guests to Shinagawa Station,  while the remaining two continued on to Nagoya Station to ensure that the luggage arrangements did not cause any inconvenience. (JR kindly accepted not to pay the bullet train fee,  and requested us to pay only the entrance fee.)

Upon arrival at Shin-Osaka Station,  staff from Patina Osaka were scheduled to meet the guests. A thorough handover was conducted,  and the guests were able to proceed smoothly to their next hotel without any further issues.


April 20
An email was received from TA conveying the guests’ feedback. The guests expressed that the last-minute nature of the departure was stressful,  particularly for the children,  and that the experience was disappointing. They requested a refund of the transportation fee.

GSAM agreed to waive the vehicle charge,  while proposing instead to charge a manning fee equivalent to the original transportation cost.


April 21
A response was received from TA expressing appreciation for the support provided by the hotel and confirming that no further refund would be requested.

GSAM subsequently sent a follow-up email,  once again apologizing for the inconvenience caused during the stay and expressing gratitude for the guests’ understanding.

Make It Right:
GSAM demanded Hinomaru Limousine to pay the total fee JPY 5, 740 for three taxies fee from PTK to Tokyo Station and the entrance fee.
The in-charge in Hinomaru understood the situation and accepted to return to PTK by cash on 23rd or 24th in Apr.

rows.Incident Description: At 15:20, the guest contacted the Bell Desk stating they were unable to locate the greeter and the arranged car at Narita Airport.
rows.Subject: 1104 | Ms. Roselle Marie Garvida | Hotel Limousine ll Not booking the car due to miscommunication
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Actions Taken:
-GSAM attempted to call the guest using the phone number provided,  but the guest’s phone was unable to receive domestic calls within Japan.
-GSAM requested Reservations (RES) to send a message to the guest explaining the situation with an apology via Booking.com. The guest replied to RES stating they had already taken a taxi and were en route to the hotel.
-GSAM informed AFOM and greeted the guest upon arrival. The guest expressed disappointment,  but after the situation was explained,  they understood.
-AFOM offered to reimburse the taxi fare as a gesture of goodwill,  but the guest declined.
As an alternative gesture,  AFOM and GSAM decided to provide complimentary departure service using the hotel Alphard.
 
 
Investigation:
-4/27,  9:05 – RES received a message from the guest via Booking.com and asked the Bell Desk to reply using an alternate email (Yahoo). Guest Service sent the email at 9:26.
-9:20 – RES received detailed information from the guest (flight details,  number of passengers,  luggage count),  but this information was not shared with Guest Service,  assuming GS has access to the Booking.com portal to view chat message. 
-RES asked the guest to communicate with Guest Service via email rather than Booking.com messages to ensure smoother communication.
-The guest later sent a message through Booking.com portal to RES to confirm the car. 
-RES partially shared this message with the Bell Desk. The Bell Captain asked RES whether they should proceed with the booking,  but RES advised to wait for further information. (Two agents were involved hence the misunderstanding)
-Guest Service did not receive any direct email from the guest nor any clear instruction from RES.
-As a result,  when the guest arrived at Narita Airport,  they contacted the Bell Desk because they could not locate the greeter.
 
 
Make it Right:
-Seasonal amenity were arranged to guest room as an apology. 
-To prevent future misunderstandings regarding arrival and departure arrangements,  all departments must ensure accurate and complete information is shared promptly and consistently.
-RES team to review who has access to the OTA portal and have the same understanding across the team.
